reason: The proposal requires an effective per-node manifest for image/checkpoint/overlay/draft/tokenizer plus a semantic oracle and per-rank progress contract. Existing runtime compatibility checks do not define those artifacts or the canary oracle. Adding a speculative manifest/schema would invent product inputs, so implementation waits for that contract.

The cited patches and refactors span external commits, symbols, draft modes, modalities, and image branches that were not audited. A trusted mapping from exact patch identity to effective code state and supported modes is missing; no status detector or canary rules should be invented before that contract.

The local telemetry instrument does not establish dew point, airflow, condensation risk, or a comparable workload baseline. This requires controlled physical cooling and long-soak work with OEM limits; no cooling or workload intervention was performed.

The report names tokenizer/checkpoint/patch failure modes, but the exact affected and corrected artifacts, digest, expected token sentinels, and modality inputs are not available as a trusted local capture. Existing runtime preflight does not inspect tokenizer behavior; no tokenizer/model tests were run.

The candidate is a global allocator monkeypatch loaded via .pth, with a required prior commit and later patch-supersession reports. External code, wheel/image identity, symbol scope, and memory lifetime semantics are unaudited. A source-of-truth patch-state contract is needed before a detector can safely classify it.
